# Common Usage

## Lists

Unnumbered lists are generated automatically in Quarto by starting a line with `-` or `*` or `+`.

- So a list can start like this,
- Then continues
     + And a sublist can start after that
          * And even more.
          
1. Numbered lists are the same
     i. And subnumbered lists
          a. And more.
          
## Tables

Tables are separated using `|` with alignments `:--:`.

| Right | Left | Default | Centre |
|------:|:-----|---------|:------:|
|   12  |  12  |    12   |    12  |
|  123  |  123 |   123   |   123  |
|    1  |    1 |     1   |     1  |

## Callout Blocks

Each callout block style has its own reserved syntax.

:::{.callout-note}
Note nte
:::

:::{.callout-warning}
Warning wrn
:::

:::{.callout-important}
Important imp
:::

:::{.callout-tip}
Tip tip
:::

:::{.callout-caution}
Caution cau
:::

:::{#nte-BoxLabel .callout-note}
## Note Box With Title and Reference

Note with stuff
:::

Note box with label @nte-BoxLabel.

:::{.callout-caution collapse=true icon=false}
Collapsible caution with no icon
:::

> Blockquote

## Output Specific Formats

Sometimes there are some outputs that will be displayed only for some formats only, this can be used using a code block as `.content-visible` while specifying with `when-format`.

:::{.content-visible when-format="html"}
Things that only appear in HTML version.
:::

:::{.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
Things that only appear in PDF version.
:::

:::{.content-visible when-format="docx"}
Things that only appear in docx version.
:::

## Figures

![Image caption here.  The image is clickable to enlarge.](figures/image.png "Title:  Image of some guy."){width=100% fig-align="center" fig-alt="Alternative caption" #fig-Figure}

In Figure @fig-Figure, there is a figure.

## Codes

Some codes can be displayed or executed directly in Quarto.  Not every programming language can be executed bit Python is one that can be.  Executable Python code blocks require `{python}` but non executable one start with `python`.  Code blocks can also be labelled and captioned with `lst-label` and `lst-cap`.

```{python}
#| lst-label: lst-Sample
#| lst-cap:  Sample caption for code.

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

S = 0

for n in range(1,10):
    S = S+n
    plt.plot(n,S,'.k',ms=10)

print(S)
```

Codes can be referenced using `@`, like @lst-Sample.
